title: Reviewing Adequacy of 300 Megawatt Additional Data Centre Capacity Baseline in Roadmap
what_it_is: Reviewing Adequacy of 300 Megawatt Additional Data Centre Capacity Baseline in Roadmap

sections.label: Data centre capacity and roadmap
sections.summary: Asked whether the 300 megawatts baseline in the Green Data Centre Roadmap will be reviewed and whether more data centres are expected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information in view of the national push for AI adoption (a) whether the Ministry will review the baseline of 300 megawatts additional data centre capacity outlined in the Green Data Centre Roadmap; and (b) other than the four new data centres recently announced, whether more data centres will be expected in the near future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Over the years, Singapore has grown considerable data centre capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: To support our digital development plans, we will provide room for more capacity to be built in a measured and sustainable way.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: For example, the Digital Infrastructure Bill, which was recently introduced in Parliament, will mandate and uplift baseline sustainability standards for all data centres.

sections.label: Optimising value per megawatt
sections.summary: Singapore is not chasing megawatt additions but optimising value per megawatt, including sustainability, resilience, digital security and strategic economic value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And to Ms Poh's second question, it is a pertinent one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We are not chasing how much megawatt we can add in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We are looking at how to optimise every value-added for every megawatt coming to Singapore, which includes raising sustainability standards, making sure they are resilient, digitally secure and making sure they add strategic economic value to Singapore.

sections.label: Disciplined calibrated capacity growth
sections.summary: New capacity is grown in a disciplined and calibrated way, adding value, sustainability and meeting high efficiency requirements, per the Digital Infrastructure Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We do so in a disciplined and calibrated way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And that is at the heart of the Digital Infrastructure Act, which has been tabled in Parliament for First Reading yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We are growing new capacity in a disciplined and calibrated way, making sure that whatever new capacity comes in adds value to Singapore and is sustainable, and meets the high requirements on efficiency.
